subject: Intermittent partial-generation stalls impacting Medivance workflows
messages:
From: Lydia Matthews <lydia@medivance.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>; Medivance Support <support@medivance.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <atorres@medivance.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:03:12 -0400
Subject: Re: sudden stalls on generation — user impact on order-entry

Hi Kimberly / Redwood team,

We started seeing a spike in partial-generation stalls around 08:58 ET this morning. Our order-entry UI is intermittently receiving truncated/empty responses (the call succeeds but the response stream hangs for 12-20s before returning). This is impacting checkout throughput and a few customers have dropped out of the flow.

Sample request ids from our logs: req_20261021_0827_aa3b, req_20261021_0830_f12c, req_20261021_0839_c8d1.

We attached a small extract with timestamps and request ids (medivance_error_snippets.txt). Please let us know if this looks like something on our side or if you’re seeing a platform issue. We need an ETA — this is customer-facing.

Thanks,
Lydia Matthews
Head of Integrations, Medivance, Inc.
lydia@medivance.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:15:46 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: sudden stalls on generation — Medivance impact (triage)

Quick triage notes:
- Observed a brief spike in prefetch fanout queue latency in us-east-1 at 08:53-09:02 ET. Queue depth rose ~3.5x for ~9 minutes.
- Root symptom: routing policy between prefetch workers and generation fanout skipped a fallback path due to an ordering regression in a recently deployed change (INF-9123). That caused increased KV misses and amplified prefix cache churn; downstream generators experienced backpressure and long tail stalls for some requests.
- Mitigation applied at 09:10 ET: rolled back the ordering change and re-enabled the fallback path; we also bumped the per-worker fanout window to reduce transient contention.
- Visible improvement at 09:14 ET; most streaming stalls reduced to normal levels, small residual P95 elevation until 09:30 ET.

Attached: incident_timeline.csv (UTC/ET offsets).

Next steps: follow-up postmortem + permanent fix to routing decision logic (assigned INF-9123), and a playbook to avoid ordering regressions in that component.

Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Platform
ben@redwood.ai
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Matthews <lydia@medivance.com>, Medivance Support <support@medivance.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <atorres@medivance.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:20:03 -0400
Subject: RE: sudden stalls on generation — user impact on order-entry

Hi Lydia / Alex —

Thanks for the quick alert and the request ids — that was very helpful. Short update from our side: we observed a transient routing regression in our us-east control plane that briefly prevented an automated fallback path between prefetch and generation fanout. That led to higher cache miss amplification and a small window where some streaming calls saw long tail stalls (you reported the same 12–20s behavior).

Action taken:
- We rolled back the ordering change that introduced the regression at 09:10 ET and re-enabled the fallback path.
- We applied a temporary fanout-window increase to reduce contention.

Impact: partial-generation stalls for a subset of requests between ~08:53–09:02 ET. Visible P95 elevation until ~09:30 ET as the system rebalanced.

We’re preparing a short postmortem and a permanent fix (INF-9123) — I’ll share the link when it’s published. We apologize for the disruption; we understand the effect on your checkout flow and will offer a usage credit for the affected window.

If you have any logs or specific user IDs to correlate, please send them and we’ll include them in the incident packet.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Matthews <lydia@medivance.com>, Alex Torres <atorres@medivance.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 15:42:00 -0400
Subject: Incident wrap and postmortem link — Medivance integration (INF-9123)

Hi Lydia / Alex —

Following up with the completed incident packet for the Oct 21 partial-generation stalls. Thank you for your patience and for the quick signals — that helped us reduce impact.

Summary (short):
- Root cause: routing ordering regression in prefetch->fanout control that prevented fallback activation, causing KV cache churn and backpressure on generators.
- Mitigation: rollback of the ordering change + temporary fanout tuning (09:10 ET).
- Resolution: system returned to baseline by 09:30 ET; no follow-on recurrences observed.
- Permanent remediation: fix merged and scheduled for canary rollout in INF-9123 (ETA 2026-10-25), plus a new unit/regression test for routing policy order.

Postmortem & artifacts:
- Postmortem (draft): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/postmortems/MEDV-20261021 (postmortem-draft.pdf attached)
- Incident timeline CSV: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/postmortems/MEDV-20261021/incident_timeline.csv
- Tracking JIRA: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-9123

Offer: we will apply a one-time invoice credit covering the impacted window and will follow up with your finance contact to reconcile.

Please let us know if you’d like a short sync with the SRE team to walk the timeline and remediation.

Thanks again — we’ll keep you notified of the canary rollout and confirm once INF-9123 has finished verification.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai

Attachments: postmortem-draft.pdf
